rejected.title: Short-term and long-term effects
card: Short-term
A short-term effect is felt soon after an event and is often over quickly. Deaths in a battle or damage to a town are examples.
Long-term
A long-term effect lasts for years or generations. Changed beliefs about a nation or a shift in who holds power are examples.
What sorts an effect is how long it lasts, not how soon it starts. A long-term effect can begin straight after the event.
One event can have both kinds of effect. Some long-term effects only become clear when historians look back across many years.
rejected.remember: Sort an effect by how long it lasts. One event can have both short-term and long-term effects.

a.q: An effect began within weeks of an event and lasted for 80 years. How should a historian sort it?
opts: Long-term, because of how long it lasted
Short-term, because of how soon it began
Both kinds, because it began soon and lasted
Neither kind, because it began too early
a.why: An effect is sorted by how long it lasts, and 80 years is a long time. Calling it both kinds is tempting, but it is the event that can have both kinds of effect. Each single effect is sorted by its length.
a.clue: Does the start or the length decide it?

b.q: In 1851 gold was found near Bathurst in New South Wales. Thousands rushed there, and many newcomers stayed in the colonies. Which is a long-term effect of the gold rushes?
opts: Growth in Australia's population and cities
Crowded tent camps at the diggings
Shops at the diggings running short of tools
High prices for food at the diggings
b.why: Many newcomers stayed, so the colonies' population and cities kept growing for decades. Crowded camps, short supplies and high prices at the diggings were real effects, but they eased as the rush faded, so they were short-term.
b.clue: Which change would still be seen decades later?

a.q: Which is a long-term effect of a war?
opts: Beliefs about the nation that last for generations
Deaths among the soldiers in one battle
Damage to a bridge during the fighting
A shortage of food in the week after a siege
a.why: Changed beliefs about a nation can last for generations. The other options happened soon after events and were limited to a short period.
a.clue: Which effect is still felt long after the fighting ends?

b.q: In 1851 gold was found near Bathurst in New South Wales, and thousands rushed there within months. Which is a long-term effect of the gold rushes?
opts: Lasting growth in Australia's population and cities
Crowded camps in the first months after the discovery
Workers leaving farms to dig for gold that year
Rising prices of food at the diggings that season
b.why: Population and city growth lasted for decades and shaped the colonies. The other options describe changes that happened quickly and were limited to a short time.
b.clue: Which effect was still shaping the colonies decades later?

a.best: Beliefs about the nation that last for generations

b.best: Lasting growth in Australia's population and cities

problems.detail: The remember line says short-term effects 'come soon and fade' as a flat rule, but the card says they are 'often over quickly'. The remember line drops the hedge and sorts the two kinds more neatly than the card does.

The right option is the only one that says 'Lasting'. Every other option is tied to a short time ('that season', 'first months', 'that year'), so the word itself gives the answer away.

'Ask how soon it began' can mislead. Many long-term effects begin straight away, such as population growth that started within months of the 1851 discovery. What makes an effect long-term is how long it lasts, not how late it starts.

proposal.title: Short-term and long-term effects in history
card: Short-term
A short-term effect comes soon after an event and is usually over within months or a few years. Deaths in a battle or damage to a town are examples.
Long-term
A long-term effect carries on, or shows up, years after the event. It can last for generations, such as changed beliefs about a nation or a shift in who holds power.
Historians look at both when an effect appears and how long it lasts. Some long-term effects begin straight away and keep going. Others only show up years later.
One event can have both kinds of effect. Short-term effects show why it mattered at the time, and long-term effects show why it still matters.
proposal.remember: Short-term effects come and go soon after an event. Long-term effects carry on or appear years later.

a.q: A flood in 1890 ruined that season's crops. It also led the town to move to higher ground, where it still stands. How are these effects best described?
opts: Crop loss is short-term and the town's move is long-term
Both are short-term, because both began in 1890
Both are long-term, because the flood was so serious
Crop loss is long-term and the town's move is short-term
a.why: The crop loss came soon and was over within a season, so it is short-term. The move also began soon, but the town is still there, so it is long-term. Calling both short-term is tempting, but a long-term effect can begin straight away and keep going.
a.clue: Which effect is still there today?

opts: A new border, drawn in 1920 and still used today

Bridge repairs that were finished by the end of 1921
A rise in flu cases in the months after the war
b.why: The border began straight after the war and has lasted ever since, so it is a long-term effect. The bridge repairs are tempting because they took over a year, but they came soon after the war and were finished quickly, so they are short-term.
b.clue: Which effect still carries on many years later?

A long-term effect carries on, or shows up, years after the event. It can last for generations, such as changed beliefs about a nation or a shift in who holds power.
Historians look at both when an effect appears and how long it lasts. Some long-term effects begin straight away and keep going. Others only show up years later.
One event can have both kinds of effect. Short-term effects show why it mattered at the time, and long-term effects show why it still matters.
proposal.remember: Short-term effects come and go soon after an event. Long-term effects carry on or appear years later.

a.q: A flood in 1890 ruined that season's crops. It also led the town to move to higher ground, where it still stands. How are these effects best described?
opts: Crop loss is short-term and the town's move is long-term
Both are short-term, because both began in 1890
Both are long-term, because the flood was so serious
Crop loss is long-term and the town's move is short-term
a.why: The crop loss came soon and was over within a season, so it is short-term. The move also began soon, but the town is still there, so it is long-term. Calling both short-term is tempting, but a long-term effect can begin straight away and keep going.
a.clue: Which effect is still there today?

b.q: A war in the made-up country of Doria ended in 1920. A historian lists some of its effects. Which one is long-term?
opts: A new border, drawn in 1920 and still used today
Food shortages in the first winter after the war
Bridge repairs that were finished by the end of 1921
A rise in flu cases in the months after the war
b.why: The border began straight after the war and has lasted ever since, so it is a long-term effect. The bridge repairs are tempting because they took over a year, but they came soon after the war and were finished quickly, so they are short-term.
b.clue: Which effect still carries on many years later?
